jobs.text: Early Bengal was ruled by various kingdoms, among them Pundra, Vanga and Gauda, and at times formed part of larger empires such as the Mauryan and Gupta states. In the early seventh century King Shashanka of Gauda is often remembered as the first ruler to unite much of Bengal in a strong independent kingdom.

jobs.text: The Palas were Buddhists who supported learning. Pala artists made bronze statues and painted palm-leaf manuscripts that still survive in museums.

A century later, cheap factory cloth from Britain destroyed the muslin trade. The finest weaving was lost, but weavers today keep Jamdani alive, and UNESCO recognised it in 2013 as intangible cultural heritage.
